newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia SBI continues tailspin,ends 11.5 pct down.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia SBI continues tailspin,ends 11.5 pct down.

text.p: Slovenia's blue-chip SBI index continued its free-fall on Wednesday, tumbling 11.5 percent to take its losses to 20 percent in two days.
Traders said bearish sentiment was running rampant on the country's nascent bourse after the central bank decided to clamp down on foreign trading activity.
The SBI index ended 179.46 points lower at 1,380.66.
"Shares went down today as the market remained edgy -- the downward trend may continue for the next couple of days," said Toni Apollonio, an analyst at A Banka.
The central bank said on Tuesday that foreign investors in Slovenian shares must in future hold special trading accounts with fully licensed banks if they wanted to invest in domestic companies.
The long-term impact of this move on foreign investment remains cloudy, which in turn is triggering a rash of selling until the situation becomes clearer, traders said.
Foreigners had largely been behind the Slovenian bourse's spectacular bull run this year, driving the index to an all-time high on Monday -- up 40 percent since the beginning of this year.
But Apollonio added that if the current sell-off continues, some investors may be tempted to start bottom fishing.
Selling pressure was already showing signs of ebbing, as today's turnover tumbled to 74.3 million tolars from 545.7 million on Tuesday.
Overall 12 shares fell, two rose and two were unchanged, while another nine were untraded.
Pharmaceutical wholesaler Salus was the leading decliner, shedding 17.65 percent to 14,000 tolars on volume of 540 shares.
Preferred shares of Dolenjska bank were the biggest gainer, surging 6.62 percent to 14,500 tolars on volume of 433 shares.
